title: Configure the Google Sheets data source

blocks.content: In this milestone, you configure your Google Sheets data source with the API key you created and verify that the connection works correctly. This step establishes the authenticated connection between Grafana and the Google Sheets API.

Choosing the right authentication type ensures the data source can read the spreadsheets you need. The connection test validates that your API key is accepted and that the Google Sheets API is reachable.
To configure authentication and verify the connection, complete the following steps:

blocks.reftarget: [data-testid='data-testid Data source settings page name input field']
blocks.content:
In the **Name** field, enter a descriptive name for your data source.

For example, enter `My Google Sheets` or `Team Budget Sheet`.

> **Did you know?** The name of the data source appears on dashboard panels, so it's important to choose a meaningful name. If there are multiple data sources for a dashboard panel, the default toggle determines which data source appears by default.
Optionally, enable the **Default** toggle if you want this to be your default data source when creating new panels.

For **Authentication type**, select **API Key**.

The default is **Google JWT File**, which is used for private spreadsheets. Because this path uses a publicly shared spreadsheet, select **API Key** instead. You can expand **Configure Google Sheets Authentication** on the page for step-by-step guidance in the UI.

In the **API Key** field, paste the Google API key you created earlier.

**Tip:** Ensure you paste the complete key without any extra spaces or characters.
Optionally, set a **Default Spreadsheet ID** to pre-fill new queries with a spreadsheet you use often. You can enter an ID, paste a spreadsheet URL, or leave it empty and set the ID per query.

Click **Save & test** to save the configuration and test the connection.

A successful connection displays the message "Success".

Your Google Sheets data source is configured and connected. You can now query publicly shared spreadsheets from dashboard panels and Explore.

**Try it:** To test without your own spreadsheet, use Grafana's [public demonstration spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1TZlZX67Y0s4CvRro_3pCYqRCKuXer81oFp_xcsjPpe8/edit?usp=sharing). Add a visualization, select your Google Sheets data source, and paste the spreadsheet ID `1TZlZX67Y0s4CvRro_3pCYqRCKuXer81oFp_xcsjPpe8`. Leave **Range** empty to use the first sheet.

---
